text: More drives do NOT lead to more free throws. I looked into the data (NBA.com drives & FTA per team). It's all over the place: the Nuggets, Lakers and Bucks have few drives but are top 5 in free throws, while OKC and the Bulls have lots of drives but some of the lowest FTAs. Teams with more drives also play at higher pace, so the data should be skewed in their favour. Drives only account for a portion of free throws — for OKC, the team with the highest share, it's only 36%. Run a regression and they're actually negatively correlated; the r-squared is just 0.01, so variance in free throws is essentially unexplained by drives (about 0.02 fewer FTs per extra drive). Drives aren't created equally: Herro and Edwards both drive ~13 times a game but Herro takes finesse midrange shots while Ant powers through contact. Shot type, defensive scheme and how much contact refs allow matter far more than drives.
label: analysis
notes: Verifiable dataset + regression; strip the opinion and the evidence stands.
